In [[cryptography]], '''FEA-M (Fast Encryption Algorithm for Multimedia)''' is a [[block cipher]] developed in 2001 by X. Yi, C. H. Tan, C. K. Siew, and M. R. Syed.

With the unusually large [[block size (cryptography)|block size]] of 4096 bits, all of FEA-M's calculations operate on 64×64 binary [[matrix (mathematics)|matrices]]. Unlike most block ciphers, FEA-M does not use multiple rounds of encryption. Each block is encrypted using just two [[matrix multiplication|multiplications]] and two [[matrix addition|additions]]. The data is encrypted using a pair of [[session key]]s chosen for just that message. The [[key (cryptography)|key]] is an invertible matrix used to encrypt the session keys, and the encrypted session keys must be sent along with the ciphertext. Since only invertible matrices can be used for the key, the effective [[key size]] is about 4094.2 bits.

FEA-M is insecure; an attack found by [[Amr Youssef|Youssef]] and [[Stafford Tavares|Tavares]] (2003) recovers the secret key using only 1 [[known-plaintext attack|known plaintext]] and 2 [[chosen-plaintext attack|chosen plaintexts]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Li|first=Shujun|author2=Lo, Kwok-Tung|title=Security problems with improper implementations of improved FEA-M|journal=Journal of Systems and Software|volume=80|issue=5|pages=791&ndash;794|date=14 June 2006|doi=10.1016/j.jss.2006.05.002|arxiv=cs.cr/0509036|citeseerx=10.1.1.134.6135|s2cid=2381494 }}</ref>
